core_obligations: Algebra structure and the coefficient object (proof lines 3020-3050): sending a scheme to the value of the functor on its motive gives a contravariant functor to graded vector spaces, monoidality gives the Kunneth isomorphism, pullback along the diagonal gives a graded algebra structure, and the commutativity constraint together with the convention on graded vector spaces makes it graded commutative; invertibility of the value on the twist, together with the degree assumption, identifies the coefficient space in degree minus two and gives the formula for the twists of the cohomology, so the data (D0) and (D1) are produced.

Cycle class and degree map (proof lines 3052-3090): rational Chow groups are morphism groups from the base motive to the twisted motive of the scheme, so applying the functor and taking the image of the unit produces the cycle class map; the class of the fundamental cycle is a morphism from the twisted motive to the unit, and applying the functor in degree zero produces the degree map.

The axioms (proof lines 3092-3194): duality of the twisted motive descends to a duality of graded vector spaces, which gives finiteness of the cohomology and nondegenerate pairings identified with cup product followed by the degree map, proving axiom (A); monoidality gives axiom (B); compatibility of the cycle class with pullbacks, the projection formula, compatibility with exterior products and the behaviour of the class of the base follow from the description of the cycle class through correspondences and from the preparation lemma for the duality diagram.
proof_roadmap: Build the algebra structure and identify the coefficient object from monoidality and the degree assumption.
Produce the cycle class map and the degree map from morphism groups of motives.
Derive axioms (A), (B) and (C) from duality, monoidality and the correspondence description.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a rational linear monoidal functor from motives to graded vector spaces whose value on the twist is concentrated in degree minus two produces data (D0), (D1), (D2) and (D3) satisfying all the axioms of a Weil cohomology theory (statement lines 3009-3016). The proof (proof lines 3017-3194) constructs the cohomology algebra, the cycle class map and the degree map, and verifies the axioms using duality of motives, monoidality, and the description of cycles through correspondences. H3: a long construction with an axiom by axiom verification, written out in full.
